title: Workspace
summary: The 3D world container: every rendered part, model, and terrain lives here. Also home to the active Camera and the physics/raycast API (Workspace:Raycast).

methods.name: Raycast
methods.signature: Workspace:Raycast(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3, raycastParams: RaycastParams?) --> RaycastResult?
methods.description: Casts a ray and returns the first hit (instance, position, normal, distance) or nil. The modern raycasting API.

methods.name: GetPartBoundsInBox
methods.signature: Workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(cframe: CFrame, size: Vector3, params: OverlapParams?) --> { BasePart }
methods.description: Returns parts inside an oriented box region.

methods.name: GetPartBoundsInRadius
methods.signature: Workspace:GetPartBoundsInRadius(position: Vector3, radius: number, params: OverlapParams?) --> { BasePart }
methods.description: Returns parts inside a sphere region.

methods.name: GetPartsInPart
methods.description: Returns parts overlapping the given part's volume.

properties.name: CurrentCamera
properties.description: The camera currently used for rendering (usually the player's camera).

properties.name: SpawnLocation
properties.description: Convenience reference to the first SpawnLocation found (nil if none).

details.heading: Global name
details.body: `workspace` is a global shorthand for `game.Workspace` — both work everywhere.

explanation.whatItIs: The physical stage of your game. Anything you can see or bump into — parts, models, terrain, characters — is parented somewhere under Workspace.
explanation.whyItExists: Rendering and physics need one shared tree of 3D objects. Workspace is that tree, plus the tools to query it (rays, regions).
whenToUse: Parenting anything that should exist in the 3D world
Raycasts for shooting, line-of-sight, ground checks
whenNotToUse: For non-physical containers (settings, GUI) — use other containers
For server-only objects that shouldn't replicate to clients — use ServerStorage
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Workspace
 ├─ Map (models, parts)
 ├─ Characters (players' rigs)
 ├─ Camera (CurrentCamera)
 └─ Terrain
If it's rendered or simulated, it lives here.
```
tips: Use RaycastParams to filter what a ray can hit (FilterDescendantsInstances + FilterType)
Everything in workspace replicates to clients — don't stash secrets here
Parenting to workspace makes objects stream/replicate immediately; heavy spawns can be staged in ServerStorage first
commonMistakes: Using deprecated FindPartOnRay instead of Raycast
Forgetting Raycast needs a DIRECTION vector (magnitude = distance), not an end point
Raycasting against your own character because you forgot to exclude it in params

examples.title: A proper raycast
examples.code:
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {character}   -- ignore own character
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude

local origin = muzzle.Position
local direction = camera.CFrame.LookVector * 200   -- 200 studs max

local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, params)
if result then
    print("Hit:", result.Instance.Name, "at", result.Position,
          "distance:", result.Distance)
else
    print("Hit nothing")
end
examples.whyItWorks: The direction vector's length sets the ray's range. Excluding the shooter's character prevents self-hits at point-blank.
examples.commonMistake: Passing an end position instead of a direction: `Raycast(origin, target.Position)` travels only ~1 stud (the vector between them).
